ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)

The captioned appeal in MFA.No.202145/2018 is filed by the claimants questioning the liability fastened on the owner on the ground that the driver of the offending lorry did not possess effective driving licence and also on quantum.

The connected cross objection in MFA.Crob.No.200007/2019 is filed by the owner challenging the liability fastened on him on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have effective driving licence.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants on record and the learned counsel appearing for Insurance company.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:8408 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2019 3.

The facts leading to the case are as under:
The claimants who are the wife, children and mother of the deceased filed the claim petition for having lost one Basavaraj in a road traffic accident on 20.12.2015.
The claimants claimed that the deceased was hardly aged 35 years and was earning Rs.12,000/- per month and hence claiming to be the dependants filed the claim petition.

The Tribunal referring to the records held that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess effective driving licence and therefore, held that it is only the owner of the vehicle who is liable to satisfy compensation.
4. While determining the quantum, the Tribunal assessed the income notionally at Rs.6,000/-.
Without extending the benefit of future prospects and applying the multiplier of 15, Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.8,10,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
In all Rs.10,35,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded by the Tribunal from the date of petition till its realization.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:8408 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2019 5.

The learned counsel representing the claimants and the owner of the offending vehicle have relied on a judgment passed by a Co-ordinate Bench in MFA.200128/2018(WC) disposed of on 11.9.2024 which pertains to the same accident under consideration.
In the cited judgment, the Co-ordinate Bench, after thoroughly examining the records of the case, rejected the arguments advanced by the Insurance Company.
Specifically, the Bench referred to Exhibit P8 and concluded that the driver of the offending vehicle held a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the incident.
Consequently, the Bench reversed the Tribunal's finding on liability, holding the Insurance Company jointly and severally liable for satisfying the compensation awarded.
In light of this precedent, the current finding of the Tribunal on liability warrants reconsideration and deserves to be reversed accordingly.
Misreading of Exhibit P8 has significantly impacted the determination of liability in the present case.
Exhibit P8, being a critical piece of evidence since misinterpreted has Shri. Sanganna S/O Hanamanthray vs Smt. Devamma W/O Late Basavaraj @ ...

4 led to flawed conclusions, thereby NC: 2024:KHC-K:8408 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2019 affecting the third party rights and liabilities of the parties involved.
Since Exhibit P8 explicitly validates the driver's qualifications and this is overlooked or misunderstood has led to an erroneous finding that the driver did not possess effective driving licence.
6. On quantum, this Court on reassessing the material on record has noticed that the claimants have not substantiated the actual income of the deceased.
In absence of the income proof, the income of the deceased is notionally assessed at Rs.8,000/-, by adding 40% towards future prospects, the income is arrived at Rs.11,200/-.
By deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses and by applying the multiplier of 16, compensation under the head of loss of dependency is re- determined at Rs.11,200x1/4x12x16= Rs.16,12,800/-.
7. Under conventional heads, claimants are held entitled to Rs.1,90,000/-.
The accident is of the year 2015.

Hence, additional 10% escalation for every three years which works out to Rs.38,000/- is awarded by NC: 2024:KHC-K:8408 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2019 applying the principles laid down in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors1.
